claims.text: A large deep CNN (60M parameters, 650K neurons; 5 convolutional + 3 fully-connected layers with 1000-way softmax) trained on 1.2M ImageNet images achieves top-1/top-5 errors of 37.5%/17.0% (LSVRC-2010) and a winning 15.3% top-5 (ILSVRC-2012) vs 26.2% for the runner-up.
claims.context: NIPS 2012 full paper, sections Abstract/1/4.1; numbers are paper-reported test results.

claims.text: Bottleneck addressed: small labeled datasets and prohibitive cost of large high-resolution CNNs; mechanism stack is data scale (ImageNet) + model capacity (depth/breadth-controlled CNN with locality/stationarity priors) + efficient GPU 2D-convolution implementation + non-saturating neurons + dropout against overfitting (5-6 days on two GTX 580 3GB GPUs).
claims.context: Full-paper sections 1/3/4; the paper's own contributions list.

claims.text: What became possible: large-scale supervised visual representation learning as a reusable substrate; the paper closes by stating results should improve with faster GPUs and bigger datasets — the scaling-recipe reading.
claims.context: Section 1 closing + Section 5-equivalent discussion; supports the TS-003 recipe interpretation over novelty interpretation.

limitations.text: Single-dataset (ImageNet) scope; transfer claims require successor sources (ResNet record).
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

limitations.text: Recipe reading vs architectural-novelty reading must both be carried; the paper's own framing supports the recipe side.
